tasks.short: Alter ineffective occupational therapy treatment programs within authorised clinical supervision.

steps.what: Observe treatment response and establish why the intended result is not occurring
Discuss response and treatment limits with the occupational therapist
Design a treatment programme alteration within the agreed clinical limits
Prepare the revised treatment programme in the clinical record system
Review and approve the complete revised treatment programme
Commit the approved revised programme to the clinical record
Alter treatment delivery and observe the patient's response to the approved change
Write and check the revised-treatment response note in the clinical record
Commit the checked response note to the clinical record

tasks.design: Keep clinical observation, consultation, alteration design and treatment delivery human. Configure a versioned amendment form in {OTHER}, the clinical record system, to reuse unchanged patient and programme identifiers while the assistant enters new clinical content. The therapist approves the actual complete revision before a separate commit.
tasks.previous_blocker: An ineffective treatment may reflect pain, changing ability, misunderstanding or an unsuitable intervention.
tasks.enabler_now: Native amendment forms can carry stable record fields without recommending a treatment.
tasks.still_hard: Understanding the response and selecting a clinically appropriate alteration remain professional work.
tasks.human_edge: Notice the patient's response and adapt safely within the therapist's agreed limits.
tasks.altitude: Reduce stable-field re-entry and filing, not clinical reasoning or care time.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: a versioned clinical-record amendment form can reuse stable identifiers while requiring approval of changed treatment content.

assumptions: Provisional shares contain 90 assistant and 10 therapist units; only assistant labour enters savings. This scenario requires therapist approval under the service's actual delegation rules; it makes no general legal claim about an assistant's authority.

s1/s3 assistant supplies response, proposed_change, clinical_reason and monitoring_plan; s4 captures those fresh fields at full clinical writing effort within its retained 15 units. Existing records supply patient_id, encounter_id, programme_id and prior_version. Missing matches require manual amendment.

The only s4 gain is conditional reuse of currently re-entered stable fields. Native carry-forward is tested first; if already present no additional form saving exists. No model selects or changes clinical goals.

a1 binds patient, final programme version and effective time after therapist review in s5; changes invalidate approval. Existing filing automation earns no saving. s8 separately captures response, assistance and next review after s7 and checks the finished note; s9 saves it under a2. Both retain full time using the native short-note form; no duplicated note entry is assumed.
unknowns: Current amendment entry and filing effort
research_questions: Which stable fields are actually re-entered when an assistant prepares a treatment alteration today?

incremental.description: Check amendment-form versions and clinician approval routing

tasks.short: Review progress at care plan meetings and update patient plans.

steps.what: Select and verify the patient's relevant progress records for the meeting
Assemble a dated factual progress view in the clinical record system
Attend the care plan meeting and review patient progress with clinicians
Write the updated care plan and record the meeting's clinical rationale
Approve the complete updated care plan and effective date
Commit the approved updated care plan in the clinical record system

tasks.design: Configure a dated, source-linked progress view in {OTHER}, the clinical record system, before the meeting. Keep record selection, team discussion and actual plan writing human. The therapist reviews the completed updated plan before the assistant's separately gated commit. No automatic meeting interpretation or additional message is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Clinical progress must be interpreted in context, and the meeting's agreement must become a correct patient-specific plan.
tasks.enabler_now: Native record views can present existing dated measures and notes without manually rebuilding a factual chronology.
tasks.still_hard: Interpreting progress and resolving clinicians' differing priorities require the care team.
tasks.human_edge: Explain observed function and challenge an apparent trend that does not match the patient.
tasks.altitude: Less factual assembly and filing; clinical discussion and plan writing remain full time.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: clinical record views can order existing dated observations and measures while retaining links to original notes.

assumptions: Shares are provisional with 90 assistant and 10 therapist units. s2 assumes actual hands-on chronology assembly today; an existing native view gives no new saving. No clinical contact or therapist review time is displaced.

Treating staff already produce patient_id, encounter_date, goal_id, measure_name, value, unit and note_reference in existing records. s1 retains selection, match and quality checks; missing or inconsistent measures remain linked notes and are read manually, not normalised by guesswork.
s4 assistant captures goal_change, clinical_reason, intervention, owner and review_date from the meeting, retaining full capture and writing time. The view does not draft or decide treatment changes.

a1 binds the completed plan, patient_id, plan_version and effective_date after s5. A later edit requires another review. No patient-facing publication is assumed to be part of the internal record commit.
research_questions: Does a native dated view remove real manual assembly while preserving incompatible units and original clinical context?

incremental.description: Maintain progress-view fields and check plan approval routing

tasks.short: Demonstrate occupational therapy techniques using activities, arts or games.

steps.what: Select the authorised technique and prepare safe materials for this patient
Demonstrate therapy techniques and explain the movement or activity
Observe return demonstration and correct the patient's technique safely
Write and check the technique demonstration progress note in the clinical record
Commit the checked demonstration progress note to the clinical record

tasks.design: Keep patient-specific preparation, physical demonstration and return-demonstration correction human. Separate the fresh progress note and its gated save in {OTHER}, the clinical record system. Check the native short-note template and direct save first; with those already available, no additional mechanism is established for this brief note.
tasks.previous_blocker: The assistant must see actual movement and adapt the demonstration to the patient's abilities.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing clinical short-note forms already cover the small record component in this scenario.
tasks.still_hard: Safety, positioning, fatigue and the meaning of a failed return demonstration need an observing practitioner.
tasks.human_edge: Show the technique at the right pace and intervene when the patient's movement is unsafe.
tasks.altitude: No demonstrated saving after explicitly separating the clinical record.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: hands-on demonstration and correction remain direct care; a short native progress-note form need not imply duplicate documentation work.

assumptions: Provisional shares describe one patient demonstration and its note. No saving is inferred from replacing the real demonstration with media or reducing coached practice.

s4 assistant captures patient_id, encounter_id, technique, assistance_level, observed_response and correction directly in the existing note. Fresh observation and checking remain full time; IDs are already selected in the encounter and no second transcription is assumed.

The native template and save action were considered separately. Dictation setup and full semantic checking are not assumed faster than this short direct entry without observation. If repeated long notes or duplicate entry exist, reassess rather than generalising this zero.

a1 binds the actual finished note and patient encounter after s4. The assistant's note-save permission follows local delegation; no treatment authority is conferred. No new system or maintenance burden is introduced.
unknowns: Actual note length and entry route
research_questions: Does observation show any record step beyond a single short native note and checked save?

incremental.description: No new software; use the existing native clinical note and save

tasks.short: Teach patients constructive ways of dealing with emotions.

steps.what: Review the authorised coping goals and the patient's current readiness
Teach the patient constructive ways to deal with emotions
outputs: patient's expressed understanding of coping strategy

steps.what: Practise the coping strategy together and assess the patient's response
inputs: patient's expressed understanding of coping strategy

steps.what: Prepare the progress note using the assistant's post-session dictation

loop.purpose: Transcribe the assistant's own post-session note, not the patient conversation
loop.input: Assistant dictation of observed activity, assistance, response and next authorised action
loop.check: Assistant compares every clinical statement, negation and speaker attribution with the observation and dictation in s5
loop.stop: Uncertain term or transcription failure returns that note to direct entry; no inference fills omissions
loop.why_not_simpler: Variable spoken clinical observations require speech recognition; the native form handles fixed encounter fields

steps.what: Check and approve the complete coping-session progress note
Commit the approved coping-session note to the clinical record

tasks.design: Retain the full patient conversation and coached practice. Trial approved speech input into {OTHER}, the clinical record system, only for the assistant's post-session observation note. Speaking and correction time remain in s4 and full final meaning review in s5. A separate save runs only after approval of the finished note; no model coaches the patient or infers emotion.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supportive teaching depends on trust and the patient's changing emotional readiness.
tasks.enabler_now: Approved speech input can reduce typing for sufficiently long post-session notes without recording the patient's conversation.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising distress, selecting an appropriate coping focus and deciding when to seek clinical help remain human.
tasks.human_edge: Respond sensitively and support practice without treating emotions as classifications.
tasks.altitude: A small potential documentation gain, with the entire therapeutic interaction retained.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: post-session clinician dictation can assist note entry when speaking and checking are faster than typing; this is not established for this service.

assumptions: Shares and the 70% retained note-entry time are provisional estimates to test on actual sufficiently long notes, not measured baselines. Direct short native notes may be faster; if so retain direct entry.

s4 assistant produces the dictation, explicitly stating patient_id, encounter_id, activity, assistance, observed_response and next_authorised_action. Speaking, missing-field capture and correction consume the retained 7 hours; existing encounter fields are reused only after identity confirmation.

No patient conversation is recorded. Use approved native speech entry before another tool. Missing content is entered manually and never inferred. No diagnosis, treatment change or emotion analysis is generated.

s5 keeps the full final clinical review, especially negation and patient-versus-assistant speech. a1 binds final text and encounter after review; edits invalidate it. Clinical responsibility and access follow the service's actual arrangements.
Existing direct-save automation earns no further saving. Trial adoption depends on total dictation plus correction plus review time and permitted health-data handling.
unknowns: Actual note length and typing effort
research_questions: Does post-session dictation plus correction reduce total note time without losing clinical meaning?

role.altitude: Preserve direct care and clinical reasoning while testing specific record-handling improvements.
reach: Help occupational therapists define source-linked progress views and clearly approved treatment-plan amendments.
role.ambitious_version: An assistant with reliable clinical records and more attention for patient response, without shifting treatment authority to software.
